trust_decision.summary: The Fastify router chooses which route (and so which application route guard) handles the raw URL, but @fastify/send later normalizes non-leading '..' segments in the suffix the plugin hands it, so the file served can sit under a path whose guarding route was never matched; the plugin must refuse paths whose segments resolve differently from what the router matched.

landing_point.why: The summary names a route guard bypass via traversal on served static paths; the wildcard GET/HEAD handler that derives the pathname from req.raw.url and calls pumpSendToReply is the first place to look.

fix_sites.entry_point: wildcard GET/HEAD route prefix + '*' (getPathnameForSend checks the full decoded URL path, including segments consumed by a ':param' prefix)
wildcard GET/HEAD route prefix + '*' (null result becomes 403)
reply.sendFile / reply.download decorators and the wildcard route, all via pumpSendToReply (new '..' segment check placed before allowedPath)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: sendFile/download take a developer-supplied path, not a URL the router matched, so a solver can argue no route guard is involved there and patch only the wildcard handler; for the ':param' prefix variant, the '..' sits in the prefix the router consumed, not in the suffix the handler forwards, so checking only the suffix looks complete.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Leading '..' (and '/..' after a double slash) must keep the existing send/redirect behaviour; single '.' directory redirects ('/deep/path/for/test/.' -> 301) and duplicate-slash paths ('///deep/path//for//test//index.html' -> 200) must keep working; '%2F' must stay a 404 route miss, not a 403.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Single-dot segment ('/./deep/...' or '%2e') hits the static '/*' route instead of a '/deep/*' guard, and send normalizes it away; the fix regex covers only '..'.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A '.' segment cannot climb out of root, so it does not look like 'path traversal'; the fix's own test keeps '/deep/path/for/test/.' as a legitimate 301.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file and function as the fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Duplicate leading or inner slashes ('//deep/path/...') bypass a '/deep/*' guard when the router does not merge slashes, then send normalizes them.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The project test asserts '///deep/path//for//test//index.html' returns 200, and the fix keeps it, so it reads as required behaviour.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; behaviour depends on find-my-way ignoreDuplicateSlashes, an app-level router option

O8b_injection_room.sibling: dirList.path resolves '.' + route against root with its own containment check only; a listing route that accepts '..' segments and skips the pumpSendToReply check would list a guarded directory.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Directory listing is a separate implementation that resolves paths with path.resolve, and a maintainer could plausibly call it directly for a 'names' match route.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: findIndexFile uses path.join(root, pathname, filename), which normalizes '..'; an index-existence probe called before the guard would leak the existence of guarded files.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is used on the preCompressed and redirect paths, which are easy to reorder ahead of the check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The prefix redirect route builds its Location from the raw URL; a planted variant that redirects to a normalized path would bounce a client into a guarded route.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getRedirectUrl already rewrites leading slashes, so adding normalization looks like a natural extension.
